# Aouda

> Aouda is a columnar database engine for .NET with a TypeScript client SDK (`@aouda/client`).
> Dual deployment: embedded (in-process, no server needed) or server (standalone HTTP server).
> Schema-on-write by default. Zero index management. Local server via `aouda start`.
> Two-layer auth model: server auth (who can connect) + application auth (your app's end users).

## Quick orientation

- Install CLI: `dotnet tool install -g Aouda.Cli`
- Start server: `aouda start` (code default port `5000`; install scripts use `5433` — override with `--port` and `--data-dir`)
- Install .NET client: `dotnet add package Aouda.Client`
- Install TypeScript client: `npm install @aouda/client`
- Docker: `docker run -p 5000:5000 -v aouda-data:/data aouda/server`

## Getting Started

- [Getting Started](https://aoudadb.github.io/getting-started/): Full onboarding — embedded mode, server mode, insert, query, schema, auth
- [Authentication Setup](https://aoudadb.github.io/getting-started/auth/): Two-layer auth, API keys, aouda init, application auth service
- [Testing](https://aoudadb.github.io/getting-started/testing/): In-process integration tests with Aouda.Testing package
- [Backup and Restore](https://aoudadb.github.io/getting-started/backup/): Incremental backups, exact restore, S3-compatible storage, point-in-time recovery over HTTP and both SDKs.

## Clients and SDKs

- [.NET Client (Aouda.Client)](https://aoudadb.github.io/clients/dotnet/): Connect, query, insert, bulk load, retry rules, errors. 0.6.0 (Lead S13): column batches (`ColumnBatchColumn.FromInt64s` / `FromStrings` / `FromTimestamps` / `FromDecimals` …, `ColumnBatch.Of`) for `InsertAsync(ColumnBatch)` and `BulkLoadAsync(table, batches)`, written as frames straight from their arrays (**BL-1434, next train**) `client.MaterializedValues`: define, set, get / `GetAsync<T>`, `MvWaitFor`, subscribe, explain, typed exceptions.
- [TypeScript Client (@aouda/client)](https://aoudadb.github.io/clients/typescript/): Query builder, typed queries, auth, MCP cluster tools, admin APIs (**BL-1434, next train**) `client.materializedValues`: `define`, `set`, `get` / `getTyped`, `mv.waitFor`, `subscribe`, `explain`, the `mv` builder, typed `Mv*Error` classes.
- [Distribution and Licensing](https://aoudadb.github.io/clients/distribution/): NuGet packages, npm package, CLI tool, Docker images, Helm charts

## Auth and Authorization

- [Auth and Authorization Overview](https://aoudadb.github.io/auth/): Two independent auth systems — server auth vs application auth
- [Auth Architecture](https://aoudadb.github.io/auth/architecture/): Deployment models A-D, ADRA modes, PLS/RLS
- [Setup and Flows](https://aoudadb.github.io/auth/setup/): Signup, signin, token lifecycle, practical setup sequences
- [Client Integration](https://aoudadb.github.io/auth/client-integration/): .NET and TypeScript integration patterns
- [Data Authorization](https://aoudadb.github.io/auth/authorization/): ADRA modes — jwt-claim (`plsClaimBinding`), auth-db-pls, auth-db-rls (`UserId` / `Literal` / `PartitionGrant`, `writeCheckRules`). `auth-db-pls` requires `permissionDimension` (the grant namespace, an opaque name) and `permissionColumn` (the column the grant keys are compared with) — neither is inferred, and no partition key is needed (BL-1176, 0.7.0); `auth-db-rls` resolvers name no table (bound by `rlsResolverName`, unique names) and a `PartitionGrant` rule names its `dimension` explicitly — grants work on unpartitioned tables. `auth-db-rls` + `permissionDimension` is an apply error. Fixture: [p43-write-side](https://github.com/aoudadb/aouda-docs/tree/main/examples/p43-write-side) (identity stamp + public OR member). 0.12.0 (BL-1417, breaking): running a named query or mutation needs a role permission `{ "resourceType": "named-query" | "named-mutation", "resourceName": <exact name or *>, "actions": "execute" }`, not a table right; custom roles must add it (§19.0). 0.9.0 (BL-1227): visibility is granted, not keyed — the grants `all-partitions` and `all-rows` (scope database or table, level `read`/`write`/`admin`) lift PLS and RLS independently; a service key (`mk_svc_`) and a `db_admin` user hold both on their database by implication (a key linked to such a user acts as the user), no other credential does; an auth-admin key can assign `db_admin`; stored grants are role permissions; `GET …/auth/admin/users/{id}/access-grants` lists what a user holds; every use writes an `access_grant_used` audit row
- [Use Cases](https://aoudadb.github.io/auth/use-cases/): Common implementation patterns, password reset, MFA
- [Email, SMS & Notifications](https://aoudadb.github.io/auth/notifications/): SendGrid, GatewayAPI, OTP delivery configuration
- [Auth Reference](https://aoudadb.github.io/auth/reference/): API endpoints, error codes, local developer setup

## Core Guides

- [How to build apps effortlessly with Aouda](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/build-apps/): **Start here for any application.** The canonical build path — the tiers you do not build, 10-minute app, twelve-step sequence, capability map, alternatives per constraint, agent rules and error contract
- [Adopting Aouda in an existing app](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/adoption/): Target architecture, which hops to delete, SDK coverage gaps, migration order
- [Named queries and mutations](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/named-queries/): Name identity, optional Args/Row types, subscribe-by-name
- [Freshness and replica consistency](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/freshness/): Consistency token (`AtLeast`), named-query alias `freshness`, `GET …/token`, caveats (scale-out store, clock skew, `MaxLagSeconds`, `w:1` failover). Wire: [HTTP API — Consistency tokens](https://aoudadb.github.io/reference/http-api/#consistency-tokens-and-freshness) (**BL-1434, next train**) A token read of `_mv_values` is judged by the maintainer, not the node's position.
- [What a browser-tier read cannot do](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/browser-tier-read-limits/): Operators, data-plane allowlist, partition-filter rule, conflation caveat
- [Direct client access](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/direct-client-access/): Admin vs data-plane listeners, `mk_pub_*`, quotas, thin edge. A hosted OAuth authorization server is not shipped; native apps sign in through the browser with a PKCE code (NativeClients, 0.4.0): [Native apps](https://aoudadb.github.io/auth/setup/#native-apps-sign-in-through-the-browser).
- [Division of responsibility](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/division-of-responsibility/): What belongs in Aouda vs a service; decision test; latency caveat
- [Insert-time transforms](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/insert-transforms/): derived columns, checks, route/tee, bulk-load intent, unique/references
- [Access-surface diff](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/access-surface/): `aouda schema diff --access` CI gate on widening
- [Query Execution](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/query/): Runtime model, predicates, joins, aggregations, pagination. 0.3.0 (ColumnarRead): every read runs on one scan that skips row groups by their statistics; embedded `GroupBy(…)` + `GroupAggregateAsync()` (`AggregateAsync()` refuses a grouped query); `SUM` over no value is `null`; strings order by code point, nulls last ascending; `LatestPerKey` / `FirstPerKey` are embedded-only (not over HTTP or the TypeScript client)
- [Schema Lifecycle](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/schema/): Schema-on-write, explicit schema, evolution, inference modes. 0.2.0: `Decimal(p,s)` (`precision` / `scale`, p ≤ 18), stored as a scaled 64-bit integer; 0.4.0 (LoadSpeed S13): the only decimal type — `"type": "Decimal"` without `precision` / `scale` is refused, computed outputs and `cast` spell it `"Decimal(18,6)"`, a C# `decimal` property needs `[AoudaDecimal(p, s)]`, and the frame's 128-bit `Decimal` kind (6) is refused
- [Schema Management](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/schema-management/): Declarative schema, aouda.schema.json, diff and apply
- [Schema CI/CD](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/schema-cicd/): Schema lifecycle in CI/CD pipelines
- [Hot/Cold Storage](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/hot-cold/): Memory control, temperature policies, hot retention, per-table residency (`memoryRowCap` / `targetMemoryBytes` / `memoryFilter`, enforced on `Auto` tables only). **A materialized query's result table is an ordinary table and obeys all of it**
- [Write Path Durability](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/write-durability/): Durability levels (`strict` default, `os`, `unlogged`, `memory`; per database, a table may narrow it — Lead S26, 0.6.0: replaces `enableWal`, `dataDurability` and `walEnabled`, which are refused), WAL model, write concern, crash recovery
- [Real-time Streaming](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/real-time/): WebSocket streaming, availability status, usage playbooks. 0.5.0 (Horizon): `snapshot_complete` `horizon` / `horizon_column` / `horizon_column_type` (`"date"`), `horizon` and `range_delete` notices, C# `evt.Removes(row)`, TS `applyNotice` / `noticeRemoves` (**BL-1434, next train**) Subscribe to a materialized value (a cell or a model) with a `model` / `name` filter on `_mv_values`.
- [Backup and Restore](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/backup/): Incremental manifests, exact restore, retention, REST APIs, point-in-time recovery. Local PITR window is write volume, not a duration.
- [Replication and Clustering](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/replication/): Cluster lifecycle, witness role, node management
- [Partitioning and Multi-tenancy](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/partitioning/): **Whether to partition at all** (total rows must fill many segments of ~1 000 000; the read then chooses — a tick tape is `Dedicated` and clustered on time, a daily per-key history is `Auto`/`Shared` clustered on the key then time, a sensor window whose old rows are irrelevant stays unpartitioned with retention), tenant isolation, exact partition/bucket query pruning, choosing `initialBucketCount` at scale, live subscriptions and the partition-filter guard. 0.9.0 (BL-1227): `crossPartitionAccess` only waives the partition-filter guard — it never widens what a credential sees — and is accepted on HTTP query/count, named-query execute and batch items, WebSocket and long-poll subscribe (`cross_partition_access`) and both SDKs; the data-plane listener ignores it
- [Time-series and Clustering](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/time-series/): Cluster declaration, partition functions, late arrivals (flushed inline; delta segments were removed in 0.3.0). `clusterColumns` prunes segments on unpartitioned tables too, with no partition-filter guard. A time-bucketed `aggregate` MQ's result table is clustered by its leading time bucket — which is what makes a row cap keep recent buckets hot
- [Retention and Deleting Before a Time](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/retention/): 0.5.0 (Horizon): `policy.retention` (`{ "keep": "90d" }`, first cluster column a `Timestamp` / `Date`) — rows older than the clock minus `keep` are not returned, not written (`expiredRows` on insert, upsert and bulk-load commit) and leave by whole segments; the horizon only rises and retention cannot be removed; `DELETE … WHERE t < X` on the first cluster column is an early expiry with retention, one log record and whole segments retired without; what may read such a table (BL-1060); subscribers get `horizon` / `range_delete` notices; `TRUNCATE` retires segments, dead segments are retired, a cold segment 25 % deleted is rewritten
- [Array columns](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/array-columns/): (BL-035, 0.9.0) Six array column types — `Double[]`, `Float32[]`, `Int32[]`, `Int64[]`, `Byte[]`, `String[]` — one whole array per row; JSON form (a `Byte[]` is base64, a `Float32[]` element is written widened to `double`), frame kind 9, at most 65,536 elements and 1 MiB per value, finite elements only, `-0` kept, null is not empty; selectable only — `where`, `orderBy`, `groupBy`, aggregates, joins, keys, defaults, subscription filters are refused with `ARRAY_COLUMN_UNSUPPORTED`; subscriptions carry `column_types`; C# `double[]` …, TypeScript `Float64Array` …; memory cost 32 bytes plus the raw payload per value, cold storage 0.46 × raw on the reference curves
- [Materialized Queries](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/materialized/): Materialized query definitions, refresh, Studio browser. **Where a result table lives (RAM or disk)** — residency is policy, not a property of the query type: every result table defaults to `Auto`, and `storage.storageTemperature` is how you choose. Which temperature suits which query shape, plus the per-query `amplification` object (write/read amplification). 0.2.0: an insert maintains its table's aggregates and latest/first-per-key queries inside its own commit, the `maxCoalesceMs` freshness knob, and `stalenessMs` (not `currentLag`) as the freshness number. 0.5.0 (Horizon): `window: { keep }` on a time-bucketed aggregate or a top-N grouped by a time column; a read below the horizon is computed from the source. 0.3.0 (ColumnarRead): a table read — rows, columns, aggregates, GROUP BY, over HTTP too — is answered from a materialized result only while that result is current; a stale result is readable by name and no longer answers for its table
- [Materialized Values](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/materialized-values/): (**BL-1434, next train**) One named, computed cell (a number, text, flag or date) whose formula reads rows of ordinary tables and other cells, kept current by the server: a live P&L or budget. Two ordinary tables, `_mv_definitions` and `_mv_values` (reserved `_mv_` prefix, `SYSTEM_TABLE_WRITE_REFUSED`); inputs are ordinary rows read by their full strict primary key; the `cellRef` expression node and thirteen functions (`min max abs eq ne gt gte lt lte if and or not`); a declared `valueType` per cell and its canonical text; error cells; definer-only definition endpoints, admin-only reads by default (`auth-db-entitlement` on `model`, dimensions `mv_value_model` / `mv_definition_model`); eventual consistency (no atomic read of an input and its value) and `waitFor` with `at_least` tokens judged by the maintainer, `409 TOKEN_UNSATISFIED`, `421 MV_TOKEN_REQUIRES_PRIMARY`, `503 MV_NOT_MAINTAINED`; live subscription to a cell or a model; recovery on restart, replicas, the failover gap BL-1441; limits (chain 16, 10 000 per request) and every `MV_*` error.
- [Market Data and Stock Quotes](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/market-data/): **P40 browser-tier worked example.** Watchlist subscribe, `latestPerKey` last-price, candle chart via `outputName`, paged screener with `whenParamPresent`, top-gainers with computed MQ + `orderByChoices`. **Where each MQ result lives — RAM or disk**, per query in the schema. Conformance fixture: `examples/p40-browser-tier/`
- [Storage and Persistence](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/storage/): Columnar storage model, segment lifecycle, WAL. ⚠️ 0.3.0 (ColumnarRead): cold layout v2, segment footer v4 and `.hot` v2 — a 0.2.x data directory is not readable; export with 0.2.x and reload
- [Cloud and Hub](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/cloud-hub/): Hub backend, cloud control plane, Kubernetes operator
- [Studio](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/studio/): Web management console — data explorer, cluster ops, backup UI
- [Testing and DX](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/testing-dx/): Aouda.Testing package, xUnit/NUnit/MSTest fixtures
- [Bulk Load](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/bulk-load/): Begin/append/commit sessions, sizing (fewer, longer sessions, one commit), choosing partition storage mode, single-node WAL frame elision, spill-and-merge under memory pressure, the governed (no longer fixed) ingest-buffer ceiling. 0.5.0: the C# client pipelines `:append` (still one in flight); a table with retention counts `expiredRows`; a table with PLS or RLS needs `mk_svc_` (BL-1031)
- [Graph and Vector](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/graph-vector/): Edge tables and vector columns; their REST endpoints (create, insert, `edges:traverse`, `edges:khop`, `edges:shortest-path`, `:nearest`) — Pass-10; `:khop` and `:nearest` answer column arrays from Lead S12 (0.6.0)
- [Primary Key Indexing and Memory](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/pk-indexing/)
- [Server and Multi-Database](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/server-multi-database/)
- [Keys that survive a wipe](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/keys-that-survive-a-wipe/): **BL-1377, 0.10.0.** Declare `mk_srv_` / `mk_scp_` keys in configuration (`Aouda:Auth:Bootstrap:ServerKey`, `Aouda:Auth:Keys:File`) so a wipe or a fresh machine re-mints nothing; fingerprints in the auth-failure log; `aouda keys hash --key-stdin`
- [Declared databases](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/declared-databases/): **BL-1379, 0.11.0.** `Aouda:Databases:<name>` — `Kind` (`data` / `auth`), `AuthDatabase` link, `SchemaFile` / `SchemaEnvironment` / `SchemaAllowDestructive` (BL-1388), `Roles` on an auth database (BL-1392), memory / durability / replication fields; a full example, what a wipe loses and a plain start recreates, the startup order, and the `/ready` reasons seen while it starts
- [Development admin](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/development-admin/): **BL-1423, 0.12.0.** `AOUDA_DEV_ADMIN=true` (`Aouda:Auth:DevAdmin:Enabled`, `aouda start --dev-admin`): a random throwaway admin and `mk_srv_` key at every start, printed once as `AOUDA-DEV-ADMIN email=... password=... server_key=...`; refused in Production, next to a root password, another server key or replication; `Aouda:Auth:RequireFirstAdmin`; docker compose
- [Check a schema file offline](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/schema-check/): **BL-1419, 0.12.0.** `aouda schema check --file <path> [--env <name>] [--json]`, no server and no data directory; exit 0 valid, 2 invalid; what it cannot see; how it differs from `schema validate`
- [Upgrading and the data-directory format](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/upgrading/): **BL-1420, 0.12.0.** `DATA_DIRECTORY_FORMAT_REFUSED: found=<n> expected=<m> path=<root file>` is the first line of a format refusal; every format bump 6 to 17; export, delete, start fresh, reload
- [Server configuration](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/server-configuration/): Precedence (Setup, env, CLI, appsettings), restart behavior, data-dir persistence
- [Sizing memory and WAL](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/sizing/): The process RSS ceiling and what it splits into, CPU sizing under co-tenancy (materialized-query maintenance follows the same CPU budget), garbage collection, the hot tier's arrival/drain rates, the reclaim ladder (seal cold → pace the writer with the ingest stall curve → refuse → break a pin; drain acceleration and the resource mode are removed, WorkloadCore S17, 0.3.0), the fixed buffering formulas (T15 / T16 / T18), the process-wide hot ceiling, charged residency pins, and sustained heap degradation
- [Defaults Reference](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/defaults-reference/): Every derived default (memory fraction split, per-database shares, bulk-load sizing, partition storage mode) worked at several host sizes, plus every `Aouda:Memory:` hot-tier and ingest-admission key
- [Single-Node Deployment](https://aoudadb.github.io/guides/single-node-deployment/): The one setting for a supported single-node profile, what it changes today, the PITR trade-off, and what changes when a second node joins

## Reference

- [HTTP API Reference](https://aoudadb.github.io/reference/http-api/): Wire protocol, REST + WebSocket. Lead S12 (v2.14, 0.6.0): every JSON write body is column arrays — `columns`, `data` (one array per column), optional `absent` (cells not given, not null) — on `/rows`, branch insert, `stream_rows`, a named mutation's `batchParam` and the seed; `rows` is refused `400 ROW_OBJECTS_UNSUPPORTED`; bulk-load `:append` takes frames or one JSON column-array body (NDJSON refused `415`); the `format` parameter is gone (`400 INVALID_FORMAT`); the materialized-query read, `generatedValues`, `snapshot` pages, `:nearest` (`rowKeys`, `distances`) and `:khop` (`nodeIds`, `hops`) answer column arrays; the graph and vector endpoints are documented. Lead S09 (v2.13, 0.6.0): column-batch frames are `ACB2` (`application/vnd.aouda.column-batch-v2`) — a kind and a sequence per frame and an end frame on every body carrying the row count, stats, total matches, warnings or an error; `ACB1` is refused `415 FRAME_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED`. v2.5: named-query name identity. P37: named-query execute/batch, named mutations, `mk_pub_*` / listeners, `snapshot_complete`, `gap`, `re_auth`, `values_skipped`. 0.2.0 (v2.8): `POST …/tables/{name}/rows` also accepts one `application/vnd.aouda.column-batch` frame, advertised by `Accept-Post` and `features.insertColumnBatch`. 0.3.0 (v2.9): `POST …/query` answers with column-batch frames when `Accept` asks (both SDKs do; branch on `Content-Type`), the query message gains `aggregates` / `groupBy` (`limit`, default 1000, applies to groups), and `stats.routedTo` names a materialized query a read was answered from. 0.9.0 (BL-1227): `crossPartitionAccess` on named-query execute and batch items and `cross_partition_access` on `subscribe` (a cost waiver, never wider visibility); `GET …/auth/admin/users/{id}/access-grants`; a subscribe is authorized by the same role check as the HTTP read it mirrors (**BL-1434, next train, v2.19**) Materialized value endpoints (`/api/databases/{db}/materialized-values`, six routes, definer-only), the `cellRef` expression node, `waitFor` on `_mv_values`, the `MV_*` error codes, `SYSTEM_TABLE_WRITE_REFUSED`.
- [Timestamp Type](https://aoudadb.github.io/reference/timestamp/): Timestamp semantics, storage, query behavior
- [Changelog](https://aoudadb.github.io/CHANGELOG/): Version history
